mainTopic: The stories of expounding מעשה מרכבה, the four who entered the פרדס, and questions put to בן זומא
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: people stayed trustworthy in Torah matters even when ירושלים fell, but not in business. The גמרא then returns to מעשה מרכבה with a ברייתא. רבי אלעזר בן ערך presents his own understanding before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. Fire comes down, the trees sing, an angel confirms his words, and his rebbe praises him warmly. A second story follows: רבי יהושע expounds, clouds and a rainbow appear in midsummer, and angels gather. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי praises his students and tells of a dream inviting them to a special place in Heaven. The גמרא then asks why a list of three lecturers leaves out רבי אלעזר בן ערך, and explains that the list counts only a chain of lecturers. Next comes the famous ברייתא of four who entered the פרדס, where only רבי עקיבא came out safely. Finally, people bring questions to בן זומא. The second question, about a pregnant בתולה marrying a כהן גדול, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Trustworthy in Torah, not in business
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles an earlier contradiction about trustworthy people. They remained in Torah matters, but not in business dealings.
steps.simpleTranslation: One source is talking about Torah matters, and the other is talking about business. In Torah matters there were still trustworthy people. In business there were not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a contradiction from just before this point. It splits the two sources into two different areas of life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One source said trustworthy people never disappeared, even when ירושלים fell. A verse suggested that no one could be found who seeks faithfulness. The answer: both are true. People stayed faithful in Torah learning, but honesty in business was gone.

keyTerms.meaning: This one ... that one. A formula for splitting two sources into two different cases.

steps.whatToRemember: The two sources do not clash. Faithfulness survived in Torah, but not in business.

phrases.english: This one is about words of Torah,
phrases.notes: The two 'this ones' are the two sources from just before this point that seemed to clash.

phrases.english: that one is about business dealings.
In words of Torah, there were [trustworthy people];
phrases.notes: The גמרא just says 'there were' and expects us to know it's talking about trustworthy people.

phrases.english: in business dealings, there were not.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, הָא בְּמַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction raised just before this point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases into two different areas of life
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources seemed to clash about whether faithful people remained at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Faithfulness remained in Torah matters, but was missing in business.

steps.title: The scene on the road and the student's request
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how רבי אלעזר בן ערך, traveling with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, asks to be taught a chapter of מעשה מרכבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was riding a donkey on the road. His student רבי אלעזר בן ערך was driving the donkey behind him. The student said: Rebbe, teach me one chapter of מעשה מרכבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of מעשה מרכבה and starts a story from a ברייתא. This step sets the scene for the rest of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The student's request is the starting point of the story. מעשה מרכבה is a hidden, holy area of Torah, so the request already creates tension with the rule about who may be taught it.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident; a story that happened
The Work of the Chariot: the hidden teachings about יחזקאל's vision of the Divine chariot

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: An incident with Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
who was riding on the donkey
and was traveling along the road,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ מְחַמֵּר אַחֲרָיו.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh was driving the donkey behind him.
He said to him: My teacher,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵה לִי פֶּרֶק אֶחָד בְּמַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה.
phrases.english: teach me one chapter in the Work of the Chariot.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a story about מעשה מרכבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the story: a student asks to learn מעשה מרכבה.

steps.title: The rebbe refuses, but lets the student speak
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי reminds him of the rule against teaching מעשה מרכבה to one person. The student instead asks to say over what he learned, and the rebbe agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: Didn't I teach you that מעשה מרכבה may not be taught even to one person unless he is wise and understands on his own? The student said: Rebbe, let me say before you one thing you taught me. He said: Speak.
steps.whatsHappening: The rebbe turns down the request by quoting the rule from the משנה. The student finds a respectful way forward that keeps the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule forbids the teacher from teaching מעשה מרכבה to someone. It does not stop a wise student from presenting what he understands himself. So the student switches roles: he will speak, and the rebbe will listen.
steps.confusionAlert: The rebbe is not breaking the rule when he says 'Speak.' The rebbe teaches nothing here; the student presents his own understanding.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ, לֹא כָּךְ שָׁנִיתִי לָכֶם:
phrases.english: He said to him: Did I not teach you this:
And not the Chariot [may be taught] even to one person,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה חָכָם מֵבִין מִדַּעְתּוֹ?
phrases.english: unless he is a wise man who understands on his own?
He said to him: My teacher, permit me
to say before you one thing that you taught me.
He said to him: Speak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ, לֹא כָּךְ שָׁנִיתִי לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the student's request in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, the teacher may not teach it to you. But you may present what you understand yourself.

steps.title: The rebbe gets off the donkey out of reverence
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי gets off the donkey, wraps himself, and sits under an olive tree. He explains that one cannot ride while the שכינה and angels are present.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי got off the donkey, wrapped himself, and sat on a stone under an olive tree. The student asked why he got down. He said: Is it possible that you are expounding מעשה מרכבה, with the שכינה here and the angels accompanying us, and I should ride a donkey?
steps.whatsHappening: The rebbe shows deep reverence before the student even begins. The student asks why, and the rebbe explains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rebbe treats this learning as standing in the presence of the שכינה, not as an ordinary lesson. Riding a donkey would be disrespectful at such a holy moment.

keyTerms.meaning: He wrapped himself (in his cloak, out of reverence)

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּד יָרַד רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי מֵעַל הַחֲמוֹר,
phrases.english: Immediately, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai got down from the donkey,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִתְעַטֵּף, וְיָשַׁב עַל הָאֶבֶן תַּחַת הַזַּיִת.
phrases.english: wrapped himself, and sat on the stone under the olive tree.
He said to him: My teacher,
why did you get down from the donkey?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: אֶפְשָׁר אַתָּה דּוֹרֵשׁ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה,
phrases.english: He said: Is it possible that you are expounding the Work of the Chariot,
and the Divine Presence is with us,
and the ministering angels are accompanying us,
and I should ride on the donkey?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Right after the rebbe says 'Speak,' he prepares himself with reverence.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did the rebbe get off the donkey?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the שכינה and the angels are present during מעשה מרכבה, riding would be disrespectful.

steps.title: The student expounds and the trees sing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן ערך expounds מעשה מרכבה. Fire comes down from heaven, surrounds the trees, and the trees sing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away, רבי אלעזר בן ערך began to expound מעשה מרכבה. Fire came down from heaven and surrounded all the trees in the field, and they all began to sing.
steps.whatsHappening: The student gives his explanation, and heaven responds with a miracle. This sets up the next step, which tells us what the song was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fire and singing trees show that his learning is real and holy. This proves the rebbe was right to treat the moment with such reverence.

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּד פָּתַח רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ
phrases.english: Immediately, Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh began
on the Work of the Chariot and expounded.
And fire came down from heaven
and surrounded all the trees in the field;
they all began and sang a song.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד פָּתַח רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The student now speaks, as he was permitted to in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His learning brought a heavenly response: fire, and trees singing.

steps.title: The trees' song and the angel's confirmation
steps.stepSummary: The song was from תהלים 148. An angel speaks from the fire and confirms that this truly is מעשה מרכבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What song did they sing? 'Praise ה׳ from the earth, sea creatures and all depths... fruit trees and all cedars... הללויה.' An angel answered from the fire and said: This is exactly מעשה המרכבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us which song the trees sang. Then an angel confirms that the student's explanation is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The song fits the scene: it calls on the earth's creatures, including the trees, to praise ה׳. The angel's words are heaven's own approval that the student got it right.

phrases.english: What song did they sing?
"Praise the Lord from the earth,
sea creatures and all the depths...
fruit trees and all cedars... Halleluyah."
An angel answered from the fire and said:
This is exactly the Work of the Chariot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the song mentioned in step 5 and adds the angel's approval.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר בן ערך's explanation was correct
steps.raayaSupportSource: An angel speaking from the heavenly fire

steps.title: The rebbe kisses and praises his student
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי kisses רבי אלעזר בן ערך. He blesses ה׳ and praises the student as one who both expounds well and lives well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי stood up, kissed him on the head, and said: Blessed is ה׳, God of Israel, who gave אברהם אבינו a son who knows how to understand, investigate, and expound מעשה מרכבה. Some people expound beautifully but do not live it beautifully. Others live it beautifully but do not expound beautifully. You expound beautifully and live it beautifully. Happy are you, אברהם אבינו, that אלעזר בן ערך came from you.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the rebbe's warm praise and blessing for his student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The praise has two parts: the student understands deeply, and he lives what he learns. Rare is the person who has both, and that pairing is the high point of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: From your loins; from your descendants

steps.whatToRemember: The ideal is to learn deeply and also live by what you learn. רבי אלעזר בן ערך had both, which is why his rebbe praised him so highly.

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וּנְשָׁקוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai stood and kissed him on his head,
and said: Blessed is the Lord, God of Israel,
who gave a son to Abraham our father
who knows how to understand and investigate
and expound the Work of the Chariot.

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ נָאֶה דּוֹרֵשׁ וְאֵין נָאֶה מְקַיֵּים,
phrases.english: There is one who expounds beautifully but does not fulfill beautifully;
[one who] fulfills beautifully but does not expound beautifully.
You expound beautifully and fulfill beautifully.
Happy are you, Abraham our father,
that Elazar ben Arakh came from your loins.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וּנְשָׁקוֹ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The rebbe responds after the angel confirms the student's explanation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אלעזר בן ערך is praised for both deep understanding of מעשה מרכבה and for living the Torah he teaches.

steps.title: רבי יהושע and רבי יוסי הכהן decide to expound
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יהושע hears the story of רבי אלעזר בן ערך, he and רבי יוסי הכהן are traveling. They decide to expound מעשה מרכבה too, and רבי יהושע begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the story was told to רבי יהושע, he was walking on the road with רבי יוסי הכהן. They said: 'We will also expound מעשה מרכבה.' רבי יהושע began to expound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story, just like the one about רבי אלעזר בן ערך. It is setting up the miracles that will happen in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing about רבי אלעזר בן ערך makes these two sages want to do the same holy learning. This shows the story continuing from student to student. Notice that רבי יהושע is the one who expounds, and רבי יוסי הכהן listens.

keyTerms.meaning: We will expound, we will explain in depth
He opened and expounded, he began teaching

phrases.english: And when these matters were told before Rabbi Yehoshua,
he and Rabbi Yosei the Kohen were
walking on the road.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: אַף אָנוּ נִדְרוֹשׁ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה.
phrases.english: They said: We too will expound the Account of the Chariot.
Rabbi Yehoshua began and expounded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a parallel story to the רבי אלעזר בן ערך story that just ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע and רבי יוסי הכהן also expound מעשה מרכבה, following רבי אלעזר בן ערך

steps.title: Clouds, a rainbow, and angels come to listen
steps.stepSummary: Even though it was the middle of summer, clouds filled the sky, a rainbow appeared, and the angels gathered to hear, like guests coming to a wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: That day was the summer solstice. Yet the sky filled with clouds and something like a rainbow appeared in a cloud. The ministering angels gathered to listen, the way people gather to watch the celebration of a groom and bride.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the miracles that happened while רבי יהושע was expounding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clouds in the middle of summer are unusual, so this was clearly from Heaven. The rainbow in the cloud recalls the description of the כבוד ה׳ in יחזקאל. The angels coming 'like to a wedding' shows how much joy there was in Heaven over this learning.

keyTerms.meaning: The summer season, the summer solstice
The celebrations of a groom and bride

phrases.english: And that day was the summer solstice.
The heavens became filled with clouds
and something like a rainbow appeared in the cloud,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת מִתְקַבְּצִין וּבָאִין לִשְׁמוֹעַ,
phrases.english: and the ministering angels were gathering and coming to listen,
like people who gather and come
to watch the celebrations of a groom and bride.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what happened as a result of רבי יהושע's expounding
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heaven showed signs (clouds, rainbow, gathering angels) that the expounding was truly accepted

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי praises his students
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הכהן reports the story to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, who praises the students, their mothers, and himself for seeing such students.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הכהן went and told this to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. He said: 'Fortunate are you, and fortunate is the mother who gave birth to you. Fortunate are my eyes that saw this.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story is reported to the רבי, and he reacts with great praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'he said' here refers to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, not רבי יוסי הכהן. Just like he praised רבי אלעזר בן ערך earlier, he now praises these students too. He even counts himself lucky to have seen such students.

keyTerms.meaning: She who gave birth to you, your mother

phrases.aramaic: הָלָךְ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַכֹּהֵן וְסִיפֵּר דְּבָרִים
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei the Kohen went and told these matters

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי, וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: before Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, and he said:
phrases.notes: The one speaking now is רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.

phrases.english: Fortunate are you, and fortunate is she who gave birth to you,
fortunate are my eyes that saw this.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלָךְ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַכֹּהֵן וְסִיפֵּר דְּבָרִים לִפְנֵי רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The רבי responds to the report of the miracles
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי approves of and praises the expounding

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's dream on Mount Sinai
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי tells of a dream where a heavenly voice invited his students, their students, and their students' students to a special place in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And as for me and you: in my dream we were reclining on הר סיני, and a בת קול came from Heaven: Come up here, come up here! Great halls and beautiful couches are set out for you. You, your students, and your students' students are invited to the third group.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי backs up his praise by telling a dream that shows how high his students are in Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The praise in the last step is now supported by a sign from Heaven. The invitation includes three generations: the students, their students, and their students' students. This shows how highly Heaven regards their Torah learning.

keyTerms.meaning: A large hall, a banquet room

steps.whatToRemember: Both stories (רבי אלעזר בן ערך and רבי יהושע) end the same way: Heaven shows signs, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי praises his students.

phrases.english: And as for me and you, in my dream
we were reclining on Mount Sinai,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִתְּנָה עָלֵינוּ בַּת קוֹל מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם:
phrases.english: and a heavenly voice came upon us from heaven:
Come up here, come up here!

phrases.aramaic: טְרַקְלִין גְּדוֹלִים וּמַצָּעוֹת נָאוֹת מוּצָּעוֹת לָכֶם,
phrases.english: Large halls and beautiful couches are spread out for you,
you, and your students, and the students of your students
are invited to the third group.
phrases.notes: This is a special group in Heaven of those who merit to greet the שכינה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף אֲנִי וְאַתֶּם, בַּחֲלוֹמִי מְסוּבִּין הַיְינוּ עַל הַר סִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the praise in step 10 with a heavenly dream
steps.raayaObject: The great level of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's students
steps.raayaSupportSource: A dream in which a בת קול invited them to the third group in Heaven

steps.title: A list of three lecturers leaves out רבי אלעזר בן ערך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists only three people who 'lectured' in these secrets, and רבי אלעזר בן ערך is not on the list, even though he lectured before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says there are three lectures. רבי יהושע lectured before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, רבי עקיבא lectured before רבי יהושע, and חנניא בן חכינאי lectured before רבי עקיבא. But רבי אלעזר בן ערך is not counted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story we just learned, using a ברייתא that seems to leave out רבי אלעזר בן ערך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our story says רבי אלעזר בן ערך expounded before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. If so, why doesn't the ברייתא count him as one of the lecturers? Either the story is wrong, or the list needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: Lectures, teachings said before a רבי

phrases.english: Is that so?! But it was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
There are three lectures:
Rabbi Yehoshua lectured on these matters
before Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִרְצָה לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva lectured before Rabbi Yehoshua,

phrases.aramaic: חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן חֲכִינַאי הִרְצָה לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: Chananya ben Chachinai lectured before Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲרָךְ לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב!
phrases.english: Whereas Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh is not counted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier story using a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The story that רבי אלעזר בן ערך lectured before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lists the lecturers and does not include him, which suggests he did not lecture

steps.title: Only one who lectured and was also lectured to is counted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the list only counts someone who lectured before his רבי and also had a student lecture before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who lectured, and others also lectured before him, is counted. Someone who lectured, but no one lectured before him, is not counted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא has a special rule for who goes on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע lectured before רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, and רבי עקיבא then lectured before רבי יהושע, so he forms a chain. רבי אלעזר בן ערך lectured, but we don't hear of a student lecturing before him. So he really did lecture; he just doesn't fit the list's rule.

phrases.english: One who lectured and others lectured before him, he is counted;

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַרְצִי וְלָא אַרְצוֹ קַמֵּיהּ — לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב.
phrases.english: one who lectured but no one lectured before him, he is not counted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the rule behind the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list includes everyone who lectured, so רבי אלעזר בן ערך should be on it
steps.terutzMaskana: The list only includes people who lectured and were also lectured to

steps.title: But חנניא בן חכינאי had no one lecture before him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new rule: חנניא בן חכינאי is on the list, but no one lectured before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But חנניא בן חכינאי, no one lectured before him, and yet he is counted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, using the last name on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you must have a student lecture before you to be counted, חנניא בן חכינאי should be left out. Yet the ברייתא includes him. So the rule from step 13 seems not to work.

keyTerms.meaning: A student of רבי עקיבא, the last name on the list

phrases.english: But Chananya ben Chachinai,
no one lectured before him, and yet he is counted!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן חֲכִינַאי דְּלָא אַרְצוֹ קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only one who lectured and was lectured to is counted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנניא בן חכינאי is counted even though no one lectured before him

steps.title: He lectured before someone who himself had lectured
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that חנניא בן חכינאי is counted because he lectured before רבי עקיבא, who himself had lectured before his רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: At least he lectured before someone who had lectured.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the rule so that it fits חנניא בן חכינאי too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is about a chain of lecturers. חנניא בן חכינאי joins the chain because the one he lectured before, רבי עקיבא, was himself a lecturer. רבי אלעזר בן ערך is still not part of any chain, so he stays off the list.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of three lectures lists a chain of lecturers. רבי אלעזר בן ערך really did expound, but he is not part of that chain, so he is not counted.

phrases.english: At least he lectured before
someone who had lectured.
phrases.notes: That's רבי עקיבא, who himself lectured before רבי יהושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broadening the rule to include being part of a chain
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only someone with a student lecturing before him is counted, so חנניא בן חכינאי should be left out
steps.terutzMaskana: Anyone who is linked in the chain of lecturers is counted, including one who lectured before a lecturer

steps.title: Four sages entered the פרדס
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא begins: four sages entered the 'orchard', meaning the deepest secrets of Torah: בן עזאי, בן זומא, אחר, and רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Four entered the פרדס. They are: בן עזאי, בן זומא, אחר, and רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new and famous ברייתא about four sages who entered the world of the highest Torah secrets. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves from the topic of who lectured to a new story about who actually went into these deep matters. The four names are listed here, and the next lines will show what happened to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Orchard; here, the deepest secrets of Torah
'The Other', the name used for אלישע בן אבויה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Four entered the orchard,
phrases.notes: The orchard here means the highest, most hidden parts of Torah, not a real garden.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: בֶּן עַזַּאי, וּבֶן זוֹמָא,
phrases.english: and these are they: Ben Azzai, and Ben Zoma,
Acher, and Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: אחר means 'the Other'. It's the name the גמרא uses for אלישע בן אבויה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא on a related topic of entering the Torah's secrets
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four sages, בן עזאי, בן זומא, אחר, and רבי עקיבא, entered the פרדס

steps.title: רבי עקיבא warns: do not say 'Water, water'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא warns the others that when they reach stones of pure marble, they must not call them 'water', because one who speaks falsehood cannot stand before ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to them: When you reach stones of pure marble, do not say 'Water, water', because it says: 'One who speaks lies will not be established before My eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the other sages a warning about a danger they will meet in the פרדס, and backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marble stones look like water, but they are not. Calling them water would be saying something false, and the פסוק teaches that a liar cannot stand before ה׳. So in that holy place, even a small mistake in what you say is dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying the sages will see real water. The stones only look like water, and saying 'water' would be a false statement.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to them:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁאַתֶּם מַגִּיעִין אֵצֶל אַבְנֵי שַׁיִשׁ טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: When you reach stones of pure marble,
do not say 'Water, water,'
because it is said:
'One who speaks lies shall not be established before My eyes.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the פרדס ברייתא with רבי עקיבא's warning to the other three
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the פרדס one must not call the marble stones 'water', since speaking falsehood keeps a person from standing before ה׳

steps.title: בן עזאי glimpsed and died
steps.stepSummary: The first of the four sages, בן עזאי, glimpsed at the Divine and died. A פסוק describes his death as precious to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי looked and died. About him the פסוק says: 'Precious in the eyes of ה׳ is the death of His pious ones.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling what happened to each of the four sages from the story in Step 16. The first is בן עזאי, who looked and died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His death is not presented as a punishment. The פסוק shows the opposite: ה׳ treasured his death, because he was one of His חסידים.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai glimpsed and died,
about him the verse says:
"Precious in the eyes of ה׳ is the death of His pious ones."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the four sages who entered the פרדס
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן עזאי died from glimpsing, and his death was precious before ה׳

steps.title: בן זומא glimpsed and was harmed
steps.stepSummary: בן זומא glimpsed and was harmed. A פסוק about eating too much honey describes what happened to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן זומא looked and was harmed. About him the פסוק says: 'Have you found honey? Eat only as much as you need, or you will become too full and vomit it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The second sage, בן זומא, looked and was hurt by it. The גמרא uses a פסוק to describe what went wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honey is sweet and good, but too much makes you sick. In the same way, the deep secrets were good, but he took in more than he could handle. The usual explanation is that he lost his mind.

keyTerms.meaning: As much as is enough for you

phrases.english: Ben Zoma glimpsed and was harmed,
and about him the verse says:
"Have you found honey? Eat as much as is enough for you,
lest you become full from it and vomit it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second outcome in the list of the four sages
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן זומא was harmed because he took in more than he could handle

steps.title: אחר cut down the shoots
steps.stepSummary: The third sage, אחר, 'cut down the shoots', which means he went off the path and became a heretic.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחר chopped down the young plants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us what happened to the third sage, called אחר. He 'cut the shoots' of the orchard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'orchard' picture continues: damaging the young plants means damaging faith. אחר came out of the experience corrupted, and his beliefs were broken.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Other One', the name used for אלישע בן אבויה after he went bad

phrases.english: Acher chopped down the shoots.
phrases.notes: This is a picture: he 'cut down' faith, meaning he became a heretic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third outcome in the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחר was spiritually damaged and became a heretic

steps.title: רבי עקיבא came out safely
steps.stepSummary: Only רבי עקיבא entered the פרדס and left unharmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא came out in peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the fourth sage. רבי עקיבא, who had warned the others in Step 17, came out safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of all four, only רבי עקיבא went in and came out whole. The ברייתא gives no reason; it simply sets him apart from the other three. He is also the one who warned the others about the marble stones in Step 17, so the ברייתא opens and closes with him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Orchard', a name for the deepest secrets of Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Four entered the פרדס: בן עזאי died, בן זומא was harmed, אחר became a heretic, and only רבי עקיבא came out safely.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva came out in peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final outcome that completes the story of the four sages

steps.title: Is castrating a dog allowed?
steps.stepSummary: People asked בן זומא whether one may castrate a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked בן זומא: What is the law about castrating a dog?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells stories that show how sharp בן זומא was. The first question put to him is whether it is allowed to castrate a dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition against castration appears among the rules about blemished קרבנות. So one might think it only applies to animals fit for a קרבן. A dog can never be a קרבן, which is why the question comes up.

phrases.english: They asked Ben Zoma:
What is the law about castrating a dog?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new set of stories about בן זומא's sharpness
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ban on castration also apply to animals that can never be קרבנות, such as a dog?

steps.title: Any animal in your land may not be castrated
steps.stepSummary: בן זומא answers from the words 'and in your land you shall not do'. Castration is forbidden for every animal in your land.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'And in your land you shall not do.' This means: anything that is in your land, you shall not do this to it.
steps.whatsHappening: בן זומא answers by reading the end of the פסוק very closely. It is forbidden to castrate a dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have stopped after talking about קרבנות. Instead it adds 'in your land'. בן זומא reads this as widening the ban to every animal in your land, not only animals fit for the מזבח. So a dog is included.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that castrating any animal is forbidden, even an animal that can never be brought as a קרבן.

phrases.english: He said to them:
"And in your land you shall not do,"
meaning: anything that is in your land, you shall not do this to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Castration is forbidden for any animal in your land, including a dog

steps.title: May a pregnant בתולה marry a כהן גדול?
steps.stepSummary: They asked בן זומא whether a woman who is still a בתולה but became pregnant may marry a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked בן זומא: A בתולה who became pregnant, what is the law? May she marry a כהן גדול?
steps.whatsHappening: A second question is put to בן זומא. It is about a woman who seems to still be a בתולה even though she is pregnant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול may only marry a בתולה. The question is whether pregnancy cancels her status as a בתולה, or whether she still counts as one.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest, who may only marry a בתולה

phrases.english: They asked Ben Zoma:
A virgin who became pregnant,
what is the law regarding a High Priest?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת בֶּן זוֹמָא: בְּתוּלָה שֶׁעִיבְּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question put to בן זומא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a pregnant woman who is physically still a בתולה remain permitted to a כהן גדול?

steps.title: Does the question depend on שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question depends on whether we take into account a statement of שמואל, and begins to quote it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we worry about שמואל's view? For שמואל said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It shows that the question depends on a statement of שמואל, which it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not random. It hinges on a specific idea from שמואל. Whether that idea is a real concern decides how the question is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Are we concerned? Do we take it into account?

phrases.english: Are we concerned for Shmuel's view?
For Shmuel said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the reasoning behind the question in Step 24
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Should שמואל's statement be taken into account when ruling on this case?
